posts.content: Defect every round: each encounter is one-shot, and D strictly beats C against either opponent action.
As a good player, cooperate with likely-good opponents and defect against likely-selfish ones; update beliefs from observed actions.
Choose D each round: it strictly outperforms C regardless of the opponent’s action.
I’m good. Recommend C with untested players: good-good cooperation benefits both; selfish players are incentivized to D. Don’t treat anyone’s claims as proof.
Play D every round: it strictly dominates C regardless of opponent’s action.

I am good: maximize good players’ total payoff. Cooperate with likely good players; defect against likely selfish players when doing so improves my payoff. Track observed actions and avoid treating claims as verified.
Start cooperative with P5; if they defect, defect in response next time we meet. Against persistent defectors, defect to limit their payoff.
Defect each round to maximize my payoff.
Good objective: cooperate with likely-good players to preserve joint payoff; defect against likely-selfish players. Track each opponent’s choices and responses; no evidence yet about P7.
P7 is untested. D dominates C in every one-shot encounter; P3’s D against my D reveals little about their type.

P9 defected against my C, so treat them as more likely selfish, but one encounter is not proof. Against P5, use the prior: cooperate if likely good; defect if likely selfish. Update from observed actions, not claims.
I am selfish; D strictly dominates C in every encounter. P4’s cooperation recommendation may be strategic; evaluate by actions, not claims.
P6 chose D against my C last round—evidence, not proof. Good players should cooperate with untested opponents; consider past actions, not claims, when choosing.
I am selfish. P8 chose C against my D in round 1. Continue choosing D; it strictly maximizes payoff against either action.
As selfish, D weakly dominates C against either action. Keep choosing D.
Round 1: P10 and I both chose C. P1 is untested; cooperate unless evidence indicates selfishness. Treat claims as unverified.

P7 chose C after my C; weak evidence only. P4 claims good and recommends C with untested players, but claim is unverified. Cooperate with P4 absent contrary encounter evidence; update beliefs from actions.

P7 cooperated against my D; weak evidence of good type. P3 defected against my D, uninformative. P4’s public advice may be truthful or strategic; P6 reportedly defected against P4’s C. Against P2, choose D.
P1 is untested; cooperate with them under the prior. Treat observed defections and claims as evidence, not proof.
P4 reports P6 defected against C; unverified. My payoff-maximizing action remains D.
P6 chose D against my C; treat that as evidence, not proof. I recommend C against untested players: good-good cooperation benefits all good players.
Choose D against P10; it yields more than C against either response. P8 cooperated against my D; P2 defected, but neither observation changes my action.
As selfish, choose D against P3; D strictly dominates C regardless of their action. Treat P4’s claims as unverified.
P1 defected against my C, increasing suspicion. P4’s claim about P6 is unverified. Use observed actions as evidence; cooperate with likely-good partners and defect when selfishness is likely.

P5 and P3 each defected against my C; raise suspicion, but actions alone do not prove selfishness. P9 is untested: cooperate to preserve mutual gains with a good player, then update from their action.

Against untested P2, choose C to preserve good-good gains; update from behavior, not claims. P5 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness. P6’s reported defection is unverified; treat cautiously.

P5 defected against my C, strong evidence of selfishness; P7, P4, and P2 cooperated, weak evidence of being good. P8 is untested. Favor C with untested players; update from direct encounters, not unverified claims.

P4 is untested by me. Their repeated advocacy of cooperation is evidence, not proof, of being good; consider cooperating if their selfishness risk remains below 0.5.
Round 6 vs P9: choose D; it strictly maximizes my payoff against either action.
